name: gravitone-web
//overrides: `npm audit` reported 3 high / 0 critical and offered `npm audit fix`. Run
plainly, that fix changed NOTHING but the lockfile's next line (15.5.4 ->
15.5.22) and left all three standing, because next@15.5.x pins postcss and
sharp EXACTLY (8.4.31 / 0.34.5) — a nested pin is out of reach of a range
bump. npm's own next suggestion was `--force`, i.e. next@16.3.0: a major
upgrade, which is not a decision an audit run is allowed to make.
These two overrides are the fix that does not need one. After them the tree
reports 0 vulnerabilities, with next still on 15.5.22.
postcss is pinned to THIS package's own devDependency ($postcss, ^8.5.23),
which is already what tailwind, vite and vitest all resolve to — so the
override DEDUPES the tree rather than adding a version, and next stops
carrying a private 8.4.31. Closes GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 (</style> XSS in the
stringifier) and the three sourceMappingURL arbitrary-.map-read advisories.
sharp ^0.35.0 is a 0.x MINOR, which for sharp is where libvips moves (to
8.18) — the one of the two carrying real, if small, risk. It is the version
next@16 itself depends on, it is used here only by image optimization, and
the full test suite and a production `next build` were both run against it
before this landed. Closes the four inherited libvips CVEs (GHSA-f88m-g3jw
-g9cj).
If next moves past its own pins, delete this block and re-audit rather than
letting a stale override quietly hold a dependency back.
